reports.title: Manual on sources and methods for the compilation of COFOG statistics
reports.description: Catalogue number KS-GQ-19-010, 2019 edition. Eurostat's guidance to EU and EFTA compilers on producing government expenditure broken down by function: user requirements, the analytical framework, the bridge tables national compilers use to map their own budget classifications onto COFOG, and a country-by-country account of recording practice, with an appendix reproducing COFOG 1999 with Task Force commentary. Its own back cover: it is 'developed and agreed by the Task Force on COFOG'. Distinct from the UN classification it implements (the corpus node un-cofog-1999), and a sibling of the corpus's eu-manual-mgdd and eu-manual-qfagg.
reports.cadence_note: Three editions, stated in the manual's own text: 'This Manual on sources and methods for the compilation of COFOG statistics is in its third edition, the first having been produced in 2007 and the second in 2011.' Latest observed interval 2011 to 2019, 8 years, so releases_per_year 1/8 = 0.13, following the convention eu-manual-mgdd uses.

reports.title: Nomenclature de consommation ouest-africaine adaptée pour l'indice harmonisé des prix à la consommation (NCOA-IHPC)
reports.description: The consumption nomenclature the harmonised consumer price indices of the UEMOA member states are built on. Derived from the international COICOP and adapted for the UEMOA zone as the Nomenclature de consommation ouest africaine (NCOA), then adapted again for the index itself as NCOA-IHPC: 12 functions, 41 groups, 78 sub-groups and 126 consumption items, with imputed rents and prostitution excluded by the index's own scope. Published by AFRISTAT under the UEMOA IHPC renovation project as the companion document to the methodology guide (the corpus node afristat-ihpc-guide-2014), which lists it among the reference documents for producing the renovated index. Carries no publication date of its own: an earlier corpus note dated it 2008, which the document does not state — its text places it in the IHPC96-to-renovated-base generation (it cites COICOP alongside the SCN 1993), before the NCOA 2018 that the current base-2023 series uses.
reports.cadence_note: A nomenclature, revised only when the index is rebased; nominal rate matching the corpus's other AFRISTAT nomenclature node.

reports.title: Credit liabilities of households (table 36-10-0639-01)
reports.description: Monthly outstanding household credit liabilities — mortgage and non-mortgage debt — released from the National Balance Sheet Accounts. Statistics Canada's own product page names the source programme: 'Source (Surveys and statistical programs) National Balance Sheet Accounts'. Minted 2026-09-06 because the corpus was pointing a CMHC edge at the quarterly National Economic Accounts for figures that come from this table instead; the two are different releases of the Canadian System of Macroeconomic Accounts and the balance-sheet one is monthly.

_dropped.edge: bo-comercio-exterior -> International Merchandise Trade Statistics, Rev.2 (1998) — no node minted
_dropped.why: REFUSED 2026-09-06 (round 5, little thing 3). Round 3 deferred bo-comercio-exterior -> un-imts-2010 on edition and asked for an IMTS Revision 2 node. The document is real and live — 'Studies in Methods, Series M, No.52, Rev.2, INTERNATIONAL MERCHANDISE TRADE STATISTICS: CONCEPTS AND DEFINITIONS, United Nations, New York, 1998', https://unstats.un.org/unsd/publication/SeriesM/SeriesM_52rev2E.pdf, HTTP 200, title page read — and it is NOT minted, because nothing names it. The Bolivian citation the lead rests on says 'Informes Estadísticos M 52', which is the series number without a revision, and Series M No.52 has three of them; reading Rev.2 out of the neighbouring SCN 1993 and MBP5 citations is the researcher's inference, not the document's statement, and the edition rule refuses exactly that. Checked in the same pass and also short: Bolivia's own IMF DSBB Summary of Methodology for MET00 (api/report/getBaseSummaryofMethodologies?countryCode=BOL&categoryCode=MET00, HTTP 200) says INE 'uses the United Nations' International Trade Statistics Manual' — no title, no series number, no edition. A node with no edge would be an orphan, so none was minted. To re-open: find a document that names a revision, and the node can be minted then.

Thirteen UEMOA and CEMAC CPI edges currently point at afristat-ihpc-guide-2014 or uemoa-ihpc-note-2023 as the nearest available target, and the nomenclature minted here is the better target for any of them whose own bulletin names NCOA-IHPC rather than the guide. Burkina Faso is the visible case: the existing bf-insd-ihpc edge's basis already records that INSD's own tables are headed 'Tableau 5: Évolution des indices nationaux suivant les groupes de la NCOA-IHPC', but that sentence was read in AFRISTAT's guide, not in INSD's bulletin, and no INSD document was fetched this round. Each retarget needs the national bulletin read; this is a research pass, not a little thing. Note also the vintage split found here: Senegal, Niger and Côte d'Ivoire have already moved to NCOA 2018 for the base-2023 series and are correctly wired to un-coicop-2018, so the node minted here is the target for the older base only.
